assets.purpose: radial ring strip / alpha texture for annular ring geometry
assets.notes: Narrow transparent strip, not a 2D photograph. Apply across the ring's radial coordinate and tint in material/shader.

source_notes: Solar System Scope describes its maps as real planetary maps in equirectangular projection, based on NASA elevation and imagery data; its page notes that unmapped portions are filled with fictional terrain and that colors are tuned/saturated.

The three NASA Photojournal URLs supplied by the user are reference imagery only and were not downloaded: https://science.nasa.gov/photojournal/jewel-of-the-solar-system/ ; https://science.nasa.gov/photojournal/a-full-sweep-of-saturns-rings/ ; https://science.nasa.gov/photojournal/looking-through-the-rings/ . These are Cassini views/mosaics, not equirectangular planet maps or a radial ring strip. NASA credits on those pages: NASA/JPL-Caltech/SSI/Cornell for PIA17474; NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute for PIA11142 and PIA07513.
limitations: Planet maps are 2K (2048x1024), suitable for typical web planet rendering but not close-up zoom; Uranus and Neptune have softer, low-detail visual texture at this resolution.
The Venus asset is a cloud / atmosphere map, not a surface map.
Saturn's ring image is an alpha strip (2048x125) that needs annular UV mapping and material tinting.
Solar System Scope warns that unmapped areas use fictional terrain and colors are slightly more saturated than reference photographs.
